summary: One of the oldest Lochsa-Selway lookout sites (1915 origin), now a 1953 L-4 cab tower staffed continuously into the 2020s.

facts.design: 10 ft treated-timber tower, hip-roof L-4 cab with catwalk (built 1953)
facts.status_note: Earlier 1931 L-4 cab, relocated 100 ft downslope in 1953, still stands nearby in rough condition.

access.note: Active, staffed Forest Service lookout; rough high-clearance/4WD road or ~2 mile hike from first saddle, per idahofirelookouts.com visit report; not a public rental

visit.trail_note: Reachable by rough road (high-clearance/4WD recommended) or by hiking ~2 miles from the first saddle

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Nez Perce National Forest, Moose Creek Ranger District)

events.note: Original 12x12 ft frame cabin built on the summit
Staffed by G.A. Burrows (idahofirelookouts.com dates the cabin's construction to 1916, one year later than NHLR/firelookout.com)

Frame cabin replaced by 14x14 ft log cabin (dated 1926 by idahofirelookouts.com vs 1931 by NHLR); idahofirelookouts.com and firelookout.com also date the L-4 cab's construction to 1931, though NHLR gives 1936 for the L-4 and firelookout.com describes the L-4 as replacing the frame cabin directly rather than the log cabin
1931 L-4 cab moved ~100 ft down the mountain to make room for the present tower
Current 10 ft treated-timber tower with hip-roof L-4 cab and catwalk constructed
Registered on NHLR April 6, 2009, nominated by Gary Weber
Tom Vandewater staffing recorded as continuing through 2025 per idahofirelookouts.com staff list

evidence.supports: Original 1915 frame cabin, 1931 log cabin and L-4, 1953 relocation and current tower, NHLR date
evidence.quote: The original Coolwater Lookout on the Nez Perce National Forest was a 12'x12' frame cabin built in 1915, and replaced by a 14'x14' log cabin in 1931. In 1936 a gable-roof L-4 was built on the summit, and then moved 100' in 1953 to make room for the current hip-roof L-4 with catwalk on a 10' wood tower.

evidence.supports: 1916 construction date, staff list, old cab used as playhouse, access conditions
evidence.quote: 1916 – 12x12 frame cab with hip roof built, Staffed by G.A. Burrows

evidence.supports: 1915 founding date, heliograph relay duty, 24 miles east of Kooskia, staffed every summer
evidence.quote: Coolwater was one of the first lookout sites developed in the Lochsa-Selway country, built in 1915. One of the duties of early lookouts here was relaying heliograph messages from other lookouts that were not serviced by telephone lines.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com date the original cabin to 1915; idahofirelookouts.com dates it to 1916. Story notes the discrepancy rather than picking one.

NHLR says the log cabin replacement was 1931 and an L-4 went up in 1936 (though its own text also calls the 1953 move as happening to that 1931/1936 structure, which is internally a bit inconsistent); idahofirelookouts.com says the log cabin was 1926 and the L-4 was 1931; firelookout.com skips the log cabin entirely and says the L-4 (built 1931) replaced the frame cabin directly. Story presents all three accounts without resolving.
Only idahofirelookouts.com names G.A. Burrows as the earliest observer; firelookout.com does not mention Burrows. Story cites Burrows to idahofirelookouts.com alone.

notes_for_editor: NHLR's own description is internally a little inconsistent (mentions a 1936 gable-roof L-4 being moved in 1953 after earlier saying the log cabin replaced the frame cabin in 1931, without saying when the L-4 itself was built relative to the log cabin). idahofirelookouts.com's staff list is informal/crowd-sourced (note the comment thread correcting the Anderson staffing dates) but is the richest source for named observers.
